jobs.description: Experienced Low Observables Mission Systems Integration Engineer Company: The Boeing Company We are seeking a Low Observables (LO) Design & Integration Engineer to support design and analysis activities for stealth/low-signature systems. The engineer will perform LO material and structure design, electromagnetic analysis, integration and test support, data processing, and technical reporting. The role requires practical experience with LO materials and technologies, solid electromagnetics knowledge, and hands-on expertise with computational electromagnetic (CEM) solvers used to design and optimize LO solutions. Key Responsibilities Perform design and analysis tasks for LO materials, coatings, treatments, and structural treatments to minimize radar, infrared, and other signatures. Develop and validate LO integration concepts for aircraft/vehicle structures and subsystems, including manufacturability and testability considerations. Use CEM solvers to model, simulate, and optimize LO components and systems (e.g., surface treatments, RAM, apertures, seams, RAM-structure interactions). Perform sensitivity studies and trade-offs across materials, geometry, and integration approaches to meet system-level LO requirements. Process and analyze measured test data from laboratory and flight/field tests; compare test results to simulation and iterate designs. Produce technical documentation: detailed analysis reports, integration guidance, test plans, and summaries suitable for engineering and program management audiences. Communicate technical results and recommendations to multidisciplinary teams and support design reviews. Support manufacturing and test engineering to ensure LO design intent is preserved through fabrication and verification. Required Qualifications Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering (with a focus in Electrical, Mechanical or Aeronautical), Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry or non-US equivalent qualifications directly related to the work statement 5 or more years' related work experience or an equivalent combination of technical education and experience or non-US equivalent qualifications. 2 years experience with LO integration, design, manufacturing considerations, and test support for aerospace or defense systems. Ability to obtain Special Program Access (U.S. Only Citizenship required) Preferred Qualifications Strong understanding of electromagnetic principles relevant to radar cross section (RCS), scattering, absorption, reflection, aperture coupling, and material electromagnetic properties. Proficiency using computational electromagnetic (CEM) solvers and tools to design and optimize LO systems. Examples include but are not limited to: ANSYS HFSS, CST Microwave Studio, FEKO, SIE/PO and/or in-house CEM codes . Data processing and analysis skills using scripting and numerical tools (e.g., Python, MATLAB, NumPy, SciPy) to manipulate simulation and test datasets, perform post-processing, and generate plots. Strong technical writing and documentation skills; ability to produce clear, concise technical reports, test plans, and presentations. Ability to work collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams and communicate technical trade-offs effectively. Experience with material characterization techniques for LO materials (e.g., permittivity/permeability extraction, reflectivity/absorptivity measurements, THz/IR material characterization). Familiarity with manufacturing processes and quality controls for LO coatings and structural treatments. Experience with system-level signature analysis, multi-physics simulation, and measurement-to-model correlation workflows. Familiarity with configuration management, data versioning, and standard engineering tools (e.g., CAD, PLM systems). jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Agent Post-Training team creates the frontier agents OpenAI ships to the world. You'll develop expertise across 170+ network services built by teams spanning the globe — services that cannot be directly accessed or operated by their creators within this environment. You'll work across multiple programming languages and frameworks, diagnose issues at the code and systems level, and build full-stack solutions from design through to operational management. You'll design and implement entirely new software components, products, and services that improve operational efficiency on behalf of your network engineer customers. When technical issues arise, you'll investigate them thoroughly — diagnosing at the code or systems level, performing root cause analysis, implementing long-term fixes, and articulating technical requirements back to service owners with clarity and precision. You'll take ownership of in-house services developed specifically for this environment, carrying full-stack development responsibilities from design and implementation through to operational management and continuous improvement. You'll build reliable deployment mechanisms and monitoring solutions that address unique environmental challenges. Communication is central to your impact. You'll regularly interact with global service teams who have limited visibility into the environment, providing clear explanations of complex situations and building the relationships that ensure successful deployments and effective problem resolution. Your influence will shape how services are developed to better support this critical mission. A day in the life Your morning begins with a health check across the services your team owns — reviewing deployment pipelines, scanning monitoring dashboards, and confirming that overnight automated processes completed successfully. You notice a service deployment that partially failed and begin investigating, tracing the issue through logs and system state to identify the root cause. By mid-morning, you're deep in code. A recurring operational issue has been consuming team hours, and you're building the automation that will eliminate it permanently. You're working across an unfamiliar codebase from a global service team, reading their implementation, understanding their design patterns, and developing a solution that integrates cleanly with their architecture. This is the kind of cross-service problem-solving that makes this role uniquely rewarding. After lunch, you join a collaboration session with a service team on the other side of the world. They're preparing a major deployment and need your expertise on how their service will behave in this environment. You provide detailed technical guidance, flag potential issues based on your operational experience, and agree on a deployment plan that minimises risk. These relationships are what make complex deployments succeed. In the afternoon, you shift to development work on an in-house tool your team is building — a monitoring solution that will give network engineers better visibility into service health. You're designing the architecture, writing tests, and thinking through edge cases. It's full-stack work that stretches your engineering skills and delivers direct value to your colleagues. You end the day reviewing a pull request from a teammate and participating in your on-call handover, briefing the next engineer on current state and any items to watch. Tomorrow brings a new set of challenges — and that's exactly why you love this role. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional. About Scale
Scale builds AI systems for decisions that matter. We started out providing the data and evaluation behind many of the world's leading models, and we still work with the major frontier labs on research and post-training. Today we also build full applications: we take an organisation's own data and expertise, forward deploy alongside their teams, and build the systems they come to rely on, powered by the Scale GenAI Platform.
The Role
Defence is under pressure to adopt AI at pace. The 2025 Strategic Defence Review and the Defence AI Strategy push for AI to move from experiment to operational capability, Defence Digital and UK Strategic Command are driving digital and data programmes across the department, and the enabling organisations are being asked to field reliable systems, not pilots. Scale wants to play a foundational role in building the dependable AI applications that shift depends on.
We're looking for someone to lead that work across UK defence and the national security community. You'd own our commercial relationships across the Ministry of Defence and its enabling organisations - Defence Digital, UK Strategic Command, DE&S, and Dstl - and the broader defence and security customer base.
This is a critical role reporting directly to the new Public Sector leader. You'd carry a number, win deals yourself, and build a small team behind you as the work grows. It suits someone who has sold into defence before and knows how it actually makes decisions, not just how the org charts look.
What you'll do
Own our commercial plan and pipeline for UK defence and security
Find, shape, and close deals yourself, from the first conversation through to contract and into delivery
Use the relationships you already have across the MOD, Defence Digital, UK Strategic Command, DE&S, Dstl, and the security and intelligence community
Work the defence routes to market, and know which are worth the effort and which aren't (the Defence Sourcing Portal, DASA, JOSCAR registration, single-source arrangements, and the main CCS frameworks)
Be a credible counterpart to senior military and civil service leaders, and turn what they need into work we can actually deliver
Navigate the security clearance, accreditation, and information-handling requirements that come with defence work
Stay close to our product and delivery teams so what we sell is what we build
Hire and lead a small team over time, and help shape the wider UK public sector plan as a team with the Central Government Lead and Public Sector leader.
What we're looking for
You've sold and delivered technology or transformation work into UK defence or national security, either from a vendor or SI or from inside the MOD or the Armed Forces
You know at least one part of defence well (MOD, UK Strategic Command, DE&S, Dstl, or a single Service) and how it buys
You understand defence and public sector procurement: frameworks, tenders, single-source rules, and buying that runs through a lot of stakeholders
You've opened doors, run complex pursuits, and owned the result
You have relationships with senior people in defence
You hold, or are eligible to obtain, UK security clearance (SC as a minimum; DV desirable)
You do your best work when things are ambiguous and moving quickly
People who tend to fit this have spent years leading UK defence work at companies like Palantir, Anduril, BAE Systems, QinetiQ, Leidos or Babcock, at consultancies and systems integrators like Accenture, Deloitte, EY or PA Consulting, or in senior commercial or programme roles inside the MOD, DE&S, or the Armed Forces.
Nice to have
Experience with AI or data-heavy platforms
Regulated, mission-critical, or classified government programmes
You've built or run a small commercial team before
Why join
You'd be building this market, not maintaining it. There's no playbook to inherit, which is rather the point. The deals you win, and the way you win them, will shape how Scale works with UK defence for years.

jobs.description: Would you like to help entrepreneurs launch trucking businesses and shape who joins one of Amazon's fastest-growing transportation programs? If you have a passion for building scalable programs, improving hiring processes, and applying technology to make them better, you may be the right fit for the Sr. Program Manager, AFP Recruiting role for Amazon Freight Partner. Amazon Freight Partner (freightpartner.amazon.com) is a program that enables entrepreneurs to start and grow their trucking business alongside Amazon, with exclusive training, the ability to hire from their local communities, and long-term growth potential. This is not a traditional talent acquisition role. This role is a program management position focused on building and optimizing the systems, tools, and processes that power AFP's partner selection funnel. We are looking for a Sr. Program Manager who will own the end-to-end recruiting funnel that takes a prospective Amazon Freight Partner from initial inquiry to selection. This role manages the application review, screening, and interview processes; leads a support team and external vendors; and uses data and AI to improve the speed, quality, and consistency of partner selection. Key job responsibilities • Own the AFP recruiting funnel end to end, from inquiry, application through screening, interviews, and selection. • Design, document, and continuously optimize recruiting workflows, screening rubrics, selection frameworks. • Lead and develop a coordinator and contractor support team, setting quality standards and managing workload across the funnel. • Analyze funnel performance data to identify where candidates stall or drop off, diagnose root causes of conversion fluctuations, and implement process improvements to increase throughput. • Lead tooling automation and system integration, including screening tools, scheduling systems, and pipeline management platforms, to reduce manual effort and accelerate candidate movement through the funnel. • Manage third-party vendors, including assessment and screening tools, and hold them accountable to service levels. • Identify and deploy AI and automation to reduce manual review effort, ensuring tools comply with AI and automated decision-making regulations. • Communicate funnel performance, risks, and recommendations to senior leadership.
